caption: Table 18-13. Feeding plan summary for working and sporting dogs.
rows: Sprint activity
Feed a food with the appropriate amounts of key nutritional factors for this type of activity (Table 18-12).
Feed the right amount of food (DER = 1.6 to 2 x RER).
Check body condition frequently to assess energy balance and food dose.
Time meals and snacks correctly. Provide food or snack >four hours before activity; offer high-carbohydrate snack within 30 minutes after racing to enhance glycogen repletion.
Allow free access to water except just before racing.
Monitor hydration status frequently.
Intermediate activity (working/hunting)
Feed a food with the appropriate amounts of key nutritional factors for this type of activity (Table 18-12).

Feed the right amount of food. The food dose will be highly variable depending on duration and frequency of exercise (DER = 2 to 5 x RER) and should be calculated after assessing the amount of exercise performed.
Check body condition frequently to assess energy balance and food dose.
Time meals and snacks correctly. Feed after exercise or >four hours before exercise. Snacks should be given during exercise or at the end of breaks <15 minutes before resuming exercise.
Allow free access to water.
Monitor hydration status frequently.
Intermediate athletes (training)
Feed the same as for work (See above).
Allow adequate time to adapt to new food (>six weeks) before seasonal work.
Begin training and new food at least six weeks before seasonal work begins.
Allow free access to water.
Intermediate athletes (idle)
Feed as typical adult dog (Chapter 13).
Feed a performance food (smaller amount) or typical adult maintenance food as needed to maintain optimal body condition.
Allow free access to water.
Endurance athletes
Feed a food with the appropriate amounts of key nutritional factors for this type of activity (Table 18-12).

Feed the right amount of food. The food dose will be highly variable depending on duration and frequency of exercise (DER = 5 to 11 x RER) and should be calculated after assessing amount of exercise performed.
Check body condition frequently to assess energy balance and food dose.
Time meals and snacks correctly. Feed after exercise or >four hours before exercise. If snacks are used they should be given during or after exercise.
Allow free access to water.
Monitor hydration status frequently.
Key
DER = daily energy requirement, RER = resting energy requirement.
